title: Least-Cost Route

story.briefing: The links no longer cost the same to traverse. Find the cheapest route from the entry node to the Core itself, or establish that none exists.
story.success: Cheapest route computed. Power is rerouted along it immediately.

description: A network is given as n nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and an array of edges [u, v, w], each an undirected link between u and v costing w to traverse. Return the smallest total cost of a route from node 0 to node n-1, or -1 if no route exists. When n is 1 the answer is 0.

examples.explanation: Going through node 1 costs 5, which beats the direct link at 9.

hints: Counting hops no longer works, because a route with more links can be cheaper. You need to always extend whichever reached node currently has the lowest total cost.
Once a node is settled with the lowest cost, that cost can never improve — provided every cost is positive, which the constraints guarantee. That is what lets you finalise nodes one at a time.

Keep tentative costs, all starting at infinity except node 0 at zero. Repeatedly take the unsettled node with the smallest tentative cost, settle it, and try to improve each neighbour. A heap or sorted structure keeps the "smallest" step cheap.
